title: Vegetable Massaman Curry
subtitle: Mild Thai curry with sweet potato and chickpeas
excerpt: A gently spiced, mildly sweet Thai curry of sweet potato and chickpeas in a rich coconut sauce. Massaman is the mildest of the Thai curries, influenced by Persian and Indian spice trade routes, and is as well suited to a weeknight as to a dinner party.
sourceNotes: Massaman curry is thought to have arrived in Thailand via Muslim traders from Persia and India, which explains the use of warming whole spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, and star anise alongside the chilli paste base. The name is believed to derive from an old Thai word for Muslim.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months without the potato, which can go watery. Add fresh potato when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. An excellent batch-cook curry.

content.text: This curry contains peanuts, so it is not suitable for those with nut allergies. Frying the red curry paste in the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk tin is the key technique in Thai curry cooking; it blooms the paste and removes the raw edge. Shake the tin before opening if you prefer a uniform consistency.
Open the coconut milk tin and spoon out 3 to 4 tbsp of the thick cream from the top into the saucepan. Heat over a medium heat until the cream begins to sizzle.
Add the red curry paste and fry, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until it smells fragrant and the oil starts to separate.
Add the onion wedges and cook for 3 minutes. Add the cinnamon, cardamom, star anise, and bay leaves and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and 200ml water. Add the sweet potato and potato cubes. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes until the potato and sweet potato are completely tender. Add the chickpeas, tamarind paste, and palm sugar. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove the star anise and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve over jasmine rice, scattered with the chopped peanuts.

items.cause: Too much palm sugar, or the sweet potato is very sweet.
items.fix: Add more tamarind paste to balance; taste and adjust.

items.symptom: Potato is still firm after 20 minutes.
items.cause: Pieces were too large, or the simmer was too gentle.
items.fix: Cut pieces smaller and ensure it is a steady, gentle simmer.

items.cause: Water was added but not enough time to reduce.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 to 8 more minutes to reduce the sauce.
